intro.text: Halt! Captain Quibble owns this bridge. Passage costs three bruises to my ego.
I keep score. Conflict of interest? I prefer confluence of income.
A toll booth with swords. Finally, honest advertising.

rounds.insult: My fearsome reputation always precedes me!
answers: Then I'll fight your reputation while you catch up.
Your hat is smaller than advertised.
rounds.retort: Blast. Even my reputation has left me waiting.
rounds.hint: He has sent his reputation ahead. Challenge that instead of him.

rounds.insult: Squawk! Bridge toll: one gold coin per foot. Wings cost extra!
answers: I demand a receipt with feathers.
Put it on your bill. You've already got one.
What if I cross on my elbows?
rounds.retort: My bill? That's outrageous! It's already full of crackers!
rounds.hint: A bird has a bill. So does someone charging a toll.

rounds.insult: I can tie an enemy in seventeen different knots!
answers: Wonderful. I've been looking for a bow tie with ambition.
rounds.retort: I am a terror of the seas, not formal wear!
rounds.hint: Turn his terrifying talent into a very ordinary job.

rounds.insult: Every word spoken on this bridge belongs to me. Pay the royalties!
answers: Then these unpaid taxes belong to you too.
I shall speak exclusively in soup.
rounds.retort: Taxes? I resign! This bird is now a non-prophet organisation!
rounds.hint: If he claims every word, give him words he won't want to own.

rounds.insult: Nobody crosses my bridge until I have the last word!
answers: Last word! There, I've stolen it.
Say welcome. You get the last word; I get across.
rounds.retort: Welcome. Wait. That felt suspiciously like cooperation.
rounds.hint: Find a word that lets him win his argument and lets you cross.

miss.text: A fine sentence. Shame it arrived without a point.

win.text: My ego is thoroughly perforated. The bridge is yours to cross.
Squawk! We lost the duel, but retained the merchandising rights!
Keep them. I only wanted the right of way.

lose.text: Three dents in your composure. Come back with a sharper argument.
Right. Less swordplay, more wordplay. Let's try that again.
